insanityTips: Use EMF to confirm room location and interaction frequency, then switch to behaviour testing.
Don’t over-commit to EMF 5 unless you’ve seen consistent spikes after clear interactions.
items.name: EMF Reader
nightmareTips: Treat EMF as 'support' evidence: pair it with behaviour, not just a single reading.
Confirm the interaction first (audio/visual), then read EMF immediately.
items.summary: Use this to confirm interactions (doors, throws, switches) and to hunt for EMF Level 5.
tips: Sweep common touch points: doors, light switches, and thrown items.
If activity is spiking but EMF keeps landing on 2/3, keep checking after fresh interactions.
On bigger maps, leave it on the floor in the room so you catch surprise EMF spikes.

insanityTips: Use UV more as a behaviour tool (where it walks / where it touches) than as 'proof'.
If you’re getting consistent touches with no UV, start considering UV-less ghosts sooner.
items.name: UV Light
nightmareTips: Assume you will miss some UV if you arrive late; track touches with sound sensors if needed.
Use salt early so you can confirm footsteps even when evidence is limited.
items.summary: Check doors, windows, and light switches for fingerprints and UV footsteps.
tips: Check immediately after you hear a touch: UV evidence can time out.
Salt + UV is a strong combo for footprint confirmation.
Scan the door edge, not just the centre panel.

insanityTips: Temps is your locator, not your identity tool; switch to behaviour tests quickly.
If it keeps changing, treat that movement as information (possible roamers) rather than a bug.
items.name: Thermometer
nightmareTips: Use temps to find the room, then stop relying on them as confirmation.
If the room feels inconsistent, use sensors to confirm roaming instead of re-sweeping forever.
items.summary: Fastest way to narrow the ghost room once the building stabilises.
tips: Give the building a moment to settle; temperatures stabilise after you’ve been inside.
Look for the cold 'pocket' rather than chasing one low reading.
Re-check after room changes; roaming can drag temps around.

insanityTips: Use orbs as a fast rule-in/rule-out, then switch to hunt behaviour.
If you can’t confirm orbs, don’t stall—move on to interaction/wiki/Hunt testing.
items.name: Video Camera (Orbs)
nightmareTips: If orbs are possible, check early so you can reduce the suspect list fast.
Use a second angle on medium/large maps; one camera can miss the room.
items.summary: Used to check for Ghost Orbs and to monitor the room safely from the truck.
tips: Place the camera high and angled acrosss the room for better orb visibility.
Turn off lights in the room when checking for orbs.
If the room moves, move the camera—don’t assume orbs 'stopped'.

insanityTips: Treat writing as a bonus; don’t let it stall your identification.
If you get lots of throws but no writing, start leaning into behaviour rules earlier.
items.name: Ghost Writing Book
nightmareTips: Writing can take time; keep other tests running while you wait.
If the ghost avoids the book, use motion sensors to catch where it actually walks.
items.summary: Place in the room and wait for writing interaction.
tips: Place it where the ghost is active (near throws or door touches).
Use two books if you can, spaced apart in bigger rooms.
If nothing happens for ages, reposition after new activity spikes.

insanityTips: If Spirit Box fails, don’t loop forever—switch to hunt pattern tests.
Use it as a room-confirm tool early, then rely on behaviour.
items.name: Spirit Box
nightmareTips: Spirit Box is best used right after you find the room, before hunts become frequent.
Combine with a motion sensor so you’re asking where the ghost actually is.
items.summary: Ask questions in/near the ghost room (lights off) to check for responses.
tips: Turn off the room light and ask short questions while near the activity.
Try both alone and together depending on settings/difficulty.
If you get no response, move to where the ghost touched recently and try again.

insanityTips: Assume you won’t confirm DOTS quickly; keep behaviour tests active.
If you see consistent walking with no DOTS, consider DOTS-less ghosts sooner.
items.name: D.O.T.S Projector
nightmareTips: DOTS can be missed if coverage is poor—treat placement as a test you can improve.
Pair DOTS with sensors so you know if the ghost walked through the field.
items.summary: Project in the room and watch for DOTS silhouettes.
tips: Angle DOTS to cover the ghost's walking lanes, not just the centre.
Use a camera view to watch DOTS safely if hunts start.
Reposition after major activity shifts.

insanityTips: Crucifix is your setup tool: stabilise the room, then gather behaviour during hunts.
Don’t waste it early in a random spot—anchor it on real activity.
items.name: Crucifix
nightmareTips: Use one crucifix to secure your test zone, the other to secure your escape route.
Watch for 'burns' to confirm the ghost is still using that area.
items.summary: Prevents a hunt from starting within its radius.
tips: Place it where the ghost is most active, not where you feel safe.
On larger rooms, cover doorways and high-traffic paths.
Use it to buy time for tests, not as a permanent shield.

insanityTips: Smudge is your main survival tool; everything else is secondary.
If you’re testing speed, smudge only after you’ve observed the behaviour you needed.
items.name: Incense (Smudge Sticks)
nightmareTips: Treat smudge as 'one free escape'—plan the hiding spot first.
Don’t panic-smudge: use it when the ghost is close enough to matter.
items.summary: Temporarily repels the ghost during a chase and helps you break line of sight.
tips: Carry it when you’re doing riskier tests.
Use it to reset a chase: smudge, break line of sight, hide.
Practice the timing so it becomes muscle memory.

insanityTips: Treat salt as information: it tells you where the ghost prefers to walk.
If your only evidence is uncertain, salt + hunts gives you reliable behavioural data.
items.name: Salt
nightmareTips: Salt helps you confirm roaming patterns quickly without committing to evidence.
Use salt lanes to force the ghost to show its route.
items.summary: Confirms walking paths and pairs well with UV for footprints.
tips: Place salt on chokepoints and doorways.
Use with UV immediately after a step for footprints.
Salt is also a great 'movement detector' when evidence is limited.

insanityTips: Meds are your 'reset button' if you still need to observe a key hunt behaviour.
Don’t rely on meds—anchor on line-of-sight breaks and hiding spots.
items.name: Sanity Medication
nightmareTips: Use meds after a big sanity drain event so you stabilise the run.
If you need a long test (DOTS/writing), meds buys that time.
items.summary: Buys you more setup time by keeping hunts from starting early.
tips: Use meds to extend your setup phase if the ghost is aggressive.
If you’re already in late-game hunts, meds won’t save you alone—survival tools matter more.
Treat it as a pacing tool: meds = more time for controlled testing.
